theater: 尼羅河上游塞姆納至布痕

battle.name: 圖特摩斯一世的行動
battle.theater: 尼羅河上游塞姆納至布痕
battle.brief: 公元前1506年前後，圖特摩斯一世即位第二年就率軍溯尼羅河而上，在第四瀑布的塞姆納與布痕修起要塞、刻下界碑，把埃及的南界推回卡什以北；同時分兵向雷騰努用兵，重創老對手卡爾。卡面的埃及長矛正是這支部隊的骨幹：弓手覆蓋兩翼，矛兵居中縱深，車兵與輕騎負責衝鋒與追擊。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 圖特摩斯一世的行動是埃及新王國第十八王朝在位初期的一組雙線遠征，時間落在公元前1506年前後至公元前1493年前後；年表另有把在位期提前十餘年的高年表，以及折衷方案，說法並不一致。埃及一方以法老圖特摩斯一世為全軍最高統帥，他同時是已故法老阿蒙霍特普一世的首席軍事統帥與姻親，接位前已在軍中歷練多年；之下設有丞相、王室書記官，以及隨軍記錄行程、數目與戰果的軍事書記官。兵種包括以複合弓作戰的射手、以長矛為主的中隊步兵、持短斧與匕首的近戰兵、供法老與貴族乘用的輕型戰車，以及負責追擊殘敵的輕騎；另有數量龐大的搬運、供水與築壘人員，和沿尼羅河航行的船隊。南線的對手是史稱卡什（古實、庫施）的努比亞王國，以及西部沙漠與紅海山間的巴賈人游擊隊。北線的對手是雷騰努（黎凡特、敘利亞至巴勒斯坦一帶）的諸邦聯盟，其中卡爾是最主要的敵手，另有可能捲入的美索不達米亞勢力。戰後埃及在南方劃出以第四瀑布塞姆納為界的新邊界，北方則維持對雷騰努的鬆散影響，並未建立圖特摩斯三世那種系統化的貢賦體系。
countriesEn: The Actions of Thutmose I were a pair of linked expeditions carried out by Egypt's New Kingdom Eighteenth Dynasty early in the reign, falling between roughly 1506 BC and 1493 BC, although chronologies that shift his accession by more than a decade and compromise schemes are also in circulation. On the Egyptian side the pharaoh Thutmose I was the supreme commander; he was at once the chief military commander of the late pharaoh Amenemhotep I and his kinsman by marriage, and had served in the army for years before his accession. Beneath him stood the vizier, the royal scribes and the military scribes who recorded the itinerary, the tallies and the results of the march. The troops comprised archers using composite bows, spear-armed infantry forming the centre, close-fighting men with short axes and daggers, light chariots for the pharaoh and the nobility, and light cavalry used to run down fugitives; behind them came a great mass of porters, water-carriers and engineers, together with the river fleet. On the southern front the enemy was the Nubian kingdom known as Kerma, Kush or Kash, plus the raiding bands of the Beja in the western desert and the Red Sea hills. On the northern front stood the league of Retenu, that is the Levantine city-states of Syria and Palestine, with Charses as the principal opponent and, possibly, Mesopotamian forces drawn in at the margins. The outcome was a new southern frontier fixed at the Fourth Cataract, at Semna, while in the north Egypt kept only a loose influence over Retenu, without the systematic tribute system that Thutmose III would later impose.
people: 圖特摩斯一世，真名圖特摩斯，意為托特之子，王銜阿克珀卡拉，是阿蒙霍特普一世之妹的丈夫。承接王位前他是王室中最富軍事的成員，輔佐阿蒙霍特普一世，並曾作為王室使者率領重裝隊伍出現在卡爾面前。嗣位過程並不平順：阿蒙霍特普一世無嗣而終，繼承人名單上出現阿舒爾與門圖霍特普兩位覬覦者，圖特摩斯一世經過數年角力才把王位坐穩；阿蒙霍特普一世墓中那段由丞相所作的教誨詩，常被解讀為一位父親留給兒子的警告，暗示王位曾經沾血，年代學界至今爭議。他登基後即位第二年即發動大規模努比亞遠征，統軍沿河上溯，直抵第四瀑布。塞姆納與布痕的銘文留下可辨的指揮官名號：南方總督「卡什王之子」名下的阿蒙尼與都非，以及象萊尼的市長薩提，另有以「王之子」身分出現的將領。法老本人統率全軍、駐紮最前線，同時另派遠征隊向雷騰努方向進取，處理卡爾及其盟友。他的子女圖特摩斯二世與哈特謝普蘇特，日後接掌南疆的「卡什王之子」一系都延續其父的路線；他亦是把王室陵墓從帝王谷開山的人，葬於 KV38，後移 KV20。
peopleEn: Thutmose I, whose birth name Thutmose means son of Thoth and whose throne name was Akheperkare, was the husband of a sister of Amenemhotep I. Before he took the throne he was the most military-minded member of the royal family, serving Amenemhotep I and appearing at the head of a column of royal troops in the presence of Charses as the bearer of a royal message. The succession was not smooth: when Amenemhotep I died without issue, two claimants, Assure and Mentuhotep, appear on the list of successors, and Thutmose I needed several years of struggle to secure the kingship. The teaching-poem carved in the tomb of Amenemhotep I, which its author the vizier, is often read as a father's warning left to his son, hinting that the throne was blood-stained, and the chronology of the crisis remains disputed. In the second year of his reign he launched a great Nubian expedition, marching up the river to the Fourth Cataract. The inscriptions from Semna and Buhen preserve recognisable names of commanders: Ameni and Nehi under the title King's Son of Kush, Saty the mayor of Elephantine, and officers who appear with the title King's Son. The pharaoh commanded the army himself and encamped at the head of the column, while separate columns were sent toward Retenu to deal with Charses and his allies. His children Thutmose II and Hatshepsut, and the line of officials holding the title King's Son of Kush, carried his policy forward; he was also the first ruler to open a royal tomb in the Valley of the Kings, KV38, from which his mummy was later moved to KV20.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛屬於早王朝的裝備系統：銅或青銅矛頭以綁紮方式固定在木桿上，約公元前3200年已在埃及出現，比圖特摩斯一世的遠征早了一千五百多年。到第十八王朝，這類長矛的形制已相當標準化，矛頭窄長而有中脊，桿身長逾兩公尺，握在身側的矛兵是步兵方陣的骨幹，也是法老御前近衛與邊防駐軍的標準配備。遠征軍並非只靠長矛：射手使用複合弓，弓手列於方陣兩翼覆蓋正面，矛兵居中縱深站立，車兵與輕騎負責衝鋒與追擊，近戰兵以短斧與匕首收尾。埃及還大量使用投擲棒、圓形蒙皮盾牌與嵌銅箍的箭頭。努比亞方面的輕矛更短，適合游擊；那裡的弓手多不配盾，動作快但陣線難以維持。攻城與工程方面埃及不設攻城塔，遠征靠河船、築壘、堆石界碑與石砌要塞完成。運輸上，人力牽引的敞篷船沿尼羅河運兵運糧，陸軍則以縱隊跟隨嚮導官行軍，隊形與宿營位置每日依嚮導官標定。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card belongs to the equipment system of the Early Dynastic period: a copper or bronze head lashed to a wooden shaft, already present in Egypt around 3200 BC, more than fifteen hundred years before Thutmose I's expeditions. By the Eighteenth Dynasty the type had become standardised: a long narrow blade with a central ridge, on a shaft exceeding two metres, carried by the spearmen who formed the backbone of the infantry phalanx and the standard issue of the royal guard and of the frontier garrisons. The expeditionary army did not rely on the spear alone. Archers used composite bows, and were posted on the two flanks of the phalanx to cover its front, while the spearmen stood in depth in the centre; chariot troops and light horse charged and pursued, and close-fighting men finished with short axes and daggers. Egypt also used throw-sticks, round hide-covered shields and copper-tipped arrowheads. Nubian light spears were shorter and suited to raiding, and Nubian archers generally fought without shields, quick but unable to hold a formed line. For siege works and engineering Egypt built no siege towers: the advance was achieved by river transport, by building camps, by setting up stone boundary stelae and by masonry fortresses. Transport rested on man-hauled open boats carrying troops and grain up the Nile, while the infantry marched in columns behind the guide who marked out the route and the nightly camp.
tactics: 縱隊沿尼羅河谷北行是最可靠的戰術：船隊在河道平行推進，軍隊與糧秣在兩岸行進，每日宿營點都有計畫，後勤依賴沿途驛站、穀倉與地方屯糧，飲水與鞋襪的更替才是長途行軍的真正瓶頸。面對努比亞游擊隊，埃及的做法不是一戰定勝，而是先立界、再駐防：在第四瀑布修築塞姆納的要塞牆與塔樓，在布痕建立石砌平台、碼頭與駐軍地，把南方邊界從河道上模糊的界線變成有牆、有塔、有銘文的實體界線，再以界碑宣告越界者的處分條款。西北方向的雷騰努戰線上，埃及採用騎兵偵察與追擊殘敵的機動戰法，配合對方城邦之間的矛盾分化各邦，而不是像圖特摩斯三世那樣長期屯兵圍城。界碑的用法也很特別：把邊界刻在石頭上並附帶懲罰條款，讓軍事成果轉成可以用文字管束的權利。這種以銘文代替常駐軍的治理方式，成為後來新王國亞洲政策的模板。
tacticsEn: Marching in column up the Nile valley was the most dependable method. The fleet advanced in parallel with the river while troops and baggage moved along the banks, each night's camp was laid out in advance, and the logistics rested on way-stations, granaries and local depots; the real constraint on a long march was water and the replacement of footwear. Against the Nubian raiding bands Egypt did not try to settle the matter in a single battle, but set the frontier first and garrisoned it afterwards: at the Fourth Cataract it raised the fortress wall and towers of Semna, and at Buhen it built a stone platform, a quay and a troop station, turning a vague line on the river into a physical frontier of walls, towers and inscriptions, and then proclaimed on boundary stelae the penalties for crossing. On the north-western Retenu front the method was mobile: cavalry reconnaissance and pursuit of fugitives, and the exploitation of the rivalries among the city-states rather than the protracted siege warfare later used by Thutmose III. The stelae are distinctive in their own way: the frontier was cut into stone and given enforceable clauses, turning a military result into a right that could be administered in writing. This practice of substituting inscription for permanent garrison became the model for New Kingdom policy in Asia.
data: 地理與距離是本場行動中最可靠的一組數字。遠征起點底比斯約在北緯25度43分、東經32度39分，經阿斯旺（第一瀑布，北緯約24度）溯河而上，終點塞姆納約在北緯22度21分、東經31度47分，布痕約在北緯21度50分、東經31度30分，第四瀑布約在北緯22度；底比斯至塞姆納的直線距離約450公里，考慮河道彎曲與陸路並行，實際行程在600公里以上。年代方面，在位期一般作前1506至前1493，低年表作前1504至前1492，也有前1525至前1512的高年表，差異在十餘年之間；即位第二年即有遠征記錄是可確認的。年月一項，埃及史料沒有為這次遠征保存確切的月份，本卡採用的是傳統的開拔時節，即汛期第二月，約相當於現代的8月，屬於依避開漲水而推斷的合理安排，並非文獻明載。兵力方面，現存銘文與壁畫都沒有留下遠征兵力的確數，只能從「卡什王之子」等指揮官席位的設置、兩座主要要塞與數座小堡的分布推測其為以萬計的遠征軍，具體數字沒有可靠依據。傷亡與戰損，同樣無任何記錄可循。
dataEn: Geography and distance give the most reliable figures for this campaign. The starting point, Thebes, lies at roughly 25 degrees 43 minutes north and 32 degrees 39 minutes east; the column passed Aswan at the First Cataract, near 24 degrees north, and pushed up the river to Semna, near 22 degrees 21 minutes north and 31 degrees 47 minutes east, and to Buhen, near 21 degrees 50 minutes north and 31 degrees 30 minutes east, with the Fourth Cataract at about 22 degrees north. The straight-line distance from Thebes to Semna is about 450 kilometres; allowing for the bends of the river and for the land route running in parallel, the real column covered more than 600 kilometres. As for dates, the reign is usually given as 1506 to 1493 BC, the low chronology as 1504 to 1492 BC, and a high chronology as 1525 to 1512 BC, a spread of more than ten years; what can be fixed is that an expedition is recorded in the second year of the reign. On the month, the Egyptian record preserves no explicit month for this march: the card uses the traditional opening of the campaigning season, the second month of the inundation season, roughly August in the modern calendar, a reasonable inference from the need to avoid the flood, not a date actually written in a text. On strength, neither the inscriptions nor the tomb paintings give a firm number for the size of the expeditionary force; the existence of offices such as King's Son of Kush, of two principal fortresses and of several smaller forts only supports the guess that the column numbered in the thousands to tens of thousands, and no specific figure is securely grounded. Casualties and losses, likewise, leave no trace in any source.
cause: 直接起因是王位本身。圖特摩斯一世在阿蒙霍特普一世無嗣而終後，經過與阿舒爾、門圖霍特普等覬覦者的角力才坐穩王位，繼承的正當性需要軍事勝利來證明，而首要的敵手正是自恃有敘利亞與迦南諸邦支持的老對手卡爾。南方則是更迫切的實際威脅：史稱卡什的努比亞王國在阿蒙霍特普一世末年已把勢力推回第二瀑布一線，西部沙漠與紅海山間的巴賈游擊隊不斷襲擊商隊與河船，直接威脅底比斯的糧食與建材供應。介於兩線之間，法老還得處理一位先王留下的政治問題：是否承認對方已經建立的秩序。因此這場行動的任務非常明確，北方要重奪對卡爾一方的軍事主動權，南方要把埃及的邊界重新推回可防守的地線，並把這條線用石頭刻下來固定成不可含糊的憑據。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the kingship itself. After Amenemhotep I died without issue, Thutmose I had to fight his way past claimants such as Assure and Mentuhotep before he could sit securely on the throne, and the legitimacy of that succession had to be demonstrated by military victory. The principal enemy was the same old adversary, Charses, who counted on the backing of the Syrian and Palestinian city-states. The south was the more immediate threat: the Nubian kingdom called Kash had by the end of Amenemhotep I's reign pushed its power back to the Second Cataract, and the raiding bands of the Beja in the western desert and the Red Sea hills repeatedly struck caravans and river boats, threatening the grain and building materials on which Thebes depended. Between the two fronts the king also had to settle a political question left by his predecessor, namely whether the order his predecessor's rival had established was to be acknowledged. The task assigned to this campaign was therefore plain enough: in the north, to take the military initiative away from Charses and his allies; in the south, to push the frontier of Egypt back to a defensible line and to cut that line into stone so that it could no longer be treated as a matter of opinion.
impact: 長期看，圖特摩斯一世的行動決定了第十八王朝的國家形態。南方方面，埃及在第四瀑布建立永久駐防點，把勢力線推到尼羅河中游，第一次將史稱卡什的地區納入常設的總督體系，開啟往後三百年間埃及對上埃及與努比亞的帝國式經營；同時也把埃及與南方游擊體系的衝突固定成一條每年都要重複處理的邊防線，催生常備邊軍與遠征週期的制度。北方方面，這次行動重創卡爾的聯盟，恢復了埃及在雷騰努的信用，卻沒有建立圖特摩斯三世那樣可持續抽取的貢賦體系，說明新王國的亞洲政策仍處於以遠征維持威懾的階段。制度上最直接的遺產是界碑，把邊界刻在石頭上並附帶懲罰條款的做法，後來被第十八王朝每一代君主沿用到卡爾、幼發拉底河乃至更遠的地方。此外，他開啟了帝王谷作為王室永久陵區的傳統，而其家族的延續讓第十八王朝得以延續近兩百年。
impactEn: In the long run the actions of Thutmose I determined the shape of the Eighteenth Dynasty state. In the south Egypt established permanent garrisons at the Fourth Cataract and pushed its line of control to the middle Nile, bringing the country known as Kash under a permanent system of governors for the first time and opening three centuries of imperial management over Upper Egypt and Nubia. At the same time the confrontation with the southern raiding groups was fixed into a frontier problem that had to be dealt with year after year, which produced standing frontier troops and a rhythm of campaigning. In the north the campaign badly damaged the league headed by Charses and restored Egyptian credit in Retenu, yet it produced no sustainable tribute system of the kind Thutmose III would build, which shows that New Kingdom policy in Asia was still at the stage of deterrence by expedition rather than of permanent subordination. The most direct institutional inheritance was the boundary stela: the practice of cutting a frontier into stone and attaching penalty clauses to it was taken up by every later pharaoh of the dynasty, at Charses, on the Euphrates and further still. He also opened the Valley of the Kings as the permanent burial ground of the royal house, and the continuity of his dynasty allowed the Eighteenth Dynasty to run for nearly two hundred years.
result: 就軍事而言，行動達成了主要目標。圖特摩斯一世保住王位，並在即位第二年把南方邊界推回第四瀑布，在塞姆納修起要塞牆與塔樓，在布痕建立碼頭與駐軍地，以銘文與界碑劃定線界，委任以「卡什王之子」為名的總督接管南疆，使第四瀑布以北的努比亞第一次長期處於埃及的牢固控制之下。北方方面，卡爾及其部分盟友受到打擊，埃及在黎凡特重新取得主動，但因史料殘缺，遠征是否深入兩河流域、界碑所載的戰果究竟如何，都還有爭議，也沒有留下可持續的附庸安排。圖特摩斯一世在位約十三至十四年後去世，約前1492或前1493，葬於帝王谷的 KV38，其後移葬 KV20。整體而言，這是一場以立界、駐防、刻石取勝的行動：它沒有留下可供誇耀的大會戰，卻換來了第十八王朝得以長期經營南方與亞洲的地理前提。
resultEn: In military terms the campaign achieved its principal aims. Thutmose I kept his throne, and in the second year of his reign drove the southern frontier back to the Fourth Cataract, raising the fortress wall and towers of Semna, building a quay and a troop station at Buhen, marking the line with inscriptions and stelae, and appointing governors under the title King's Son of Kush to take charge of the southern border, so that Nubia north of the Fourth Cataract passed for the first time into firm Egyptian control. In the north Charses and some of his allies were hit and Egypt regained the initiative in the Levant, but because the sources are fragmentary there is still dispute over how far the expedition actually reached into Mesopotamia and over the results claimed on the stelae, and no durable arrangement of client states was left behind. Thutmose I died after roughly thirteen or fourteen years on the throne, around 1492 or 1493 BC, and was buried in KV38 in the Valley of the Kings, his mummy later moved to KV20. On the whole this was a campaign won by delimitation, garrisoning and inscription: it left no great pitched battle to boast of, but it bought the geographic preconditions that allowed the Eighteenth Dynasty to run its southern and Asian affairs for the long term.
